current-block: Testing if access token was revoked after authorization code reuse (the AS 'should' have revoked the access token)
comment: FINDINGS.md D3 (category: fixture). The module redeems an authorization code, REUSES it, then calls the protected resource with the access token minted on the first redemption and expects a 4xx because the AS 'should' have revoked that token on code reuse. oauth-as DOES revoke it: authorization_code_token (server.rs ~4933) detects the replay and calls Storage::revoke_token_family on the family the code minted (RFC 6749 s4.1.2, RFC 9700 s4.1.1), covered in-crate. The WARNING is logged ONLY because the fixture's protected resource (fapi2_conformance_server.rs protected_resource) validates the access token STATELESSLY -- RFC 9068 JWT signature plus RFC 9449 DPoP binding, no RFC 7662 introspection -- so a token that is still signature-valid and unexpired is accepted until expiry even though its family is revoked at the AS. A self-contained-JWT resource that does not introspect is a legitimate, spec-permitted design; revocation on code reuse is a SHOULD, and the suite logs the missing 4xx at WARNING (callAndContinueOnFailure(..., ConditionResult.WARNING)) and templates it as an expected warning, not a failure. This records the resource's stateless design honestly; it does NOT mask an AS defect. Strings captured from run 35487826596 (head c51be96), module log IYLjk64U3xLG4Zr. A recorded gap, NOT a pass: if this stops warning the runner exits 1 and this entry must be deleted.
